entries.short: Das et al., multiband monostatic+bistatic AAV RCS
entries.venue_as_printed_in_pdf: IEEE WIRELESS COMMUNICATIONS LETTERS, VOL. 15, 2026 (running head, p.3731)
entries.status_from_pdf: PUBLISHED. 'Received 3 March 2026; revised 13 May 2026; accepted 13 June 2026. Date of publication 22 June 2026; date of current version 30 June 2026.'
entries.geometry: monostatic AND bistatic, measured (anechoic far-field + non-anechoic indoor near-field)

quotes.text: The TX is fixed, whereas the RX is moved over bistatic angles theta_b = 0deg:15deg:90deg.
quotes.supports: config: genuinely mono+bistatic, our recorded claim

quotes.text: This letter develops 3GPP-compliant statistical RCS models for autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs) using monostatic and bistatic measurements acquired across multiple frequency bands (1.8 GHz-27 GHz) and bistatic angles (0deg:15deg:90deg) in both anechoic far-field and controlled indoor near-field environments.
quotes.supports: band + bistatic-angle span

entries.verdict: OUR RECORD CONFIRMED EXACTLY (IEEE WCL 2026, 15:3731-3735). Independently matches the user's tracking table.
cautions: Only the DJI Phantom 2 was newly measured here. Quote: 'The DJI Phantom 2 dataset is newly measured in this work, whereas the RCS data for the DJI Mini 2, Phantom 3, and M350 RTK were obtained from [7] and are further processed and analyzed here.' Acknowledgements thank 'Wei Fan from Southeast University for providing the measured RCS data for the DJI Mini 2, DJI Phantom 3, and DJI M350 RTK.'
*** NON-INDEPENDENCE: Wei Fan is also an author of F05 (Yuan et al.). F01 and F05 therefore share a measurement source and are NOT two independent anchors. Do not average them as if independent.

entries.short: Ziganshin et al., scattering from discretized curved bodies
entries.venue_as_printed_in_pdf: NONE - arXiv stamp only: 'arXiv:2604.05991v2 [eess.SP] 2 Jul 2026'
entries.status_from_pdf: PREPRINT. No 'accepted'/'submitted'/'to appear' statement anywhere in the PDF.
entries.geometry: bistatic near-field scattering of a PEC vehicle + canonical PEC sphere/cylinder; validated against BIRA bistatic measurements 2-18 GHz and MLFMM

quotes.text: Extended Ray-tracing Framework Sionna-RT (v0.19) [19] was used as a basic RT framework, which is open-source, parallelizable, differentiable, and provides efficient path tracing and electromagnetic field computation on triangulized geometries.
quotes.supports: Sionna is the base, version pinned

quotes.text: All objects considered in this work are assumed to be perfectly electrically conducting (PEC), as vehicle bodies can often be approximated by PEC boundary conditions.
quotes.supports: material column = PEC, matching the user's tracking table

quotes.text: Standard RT corresponds to the default Sionna-RT implementation with specular reflections and single-bounce edge diffraction, without the proposed vertex and higher-order diffraction extensions.
quotes.supports: *** an authoritative statement of what STOCK Sionna-RT does: specular + single-bounce edge diffraction only

quotes.text: In addition to the curvature-related metric, the facet size should be of several wavelengths in order to satisfy the UTD assumptions, typically E > 1.5*lambda.
quotes.supports: discretization rule - directly comparable to our mesh/few-lambda marginality caveat

entries.verdict: *** CORRECTIONS on version and on our dBsm bookkeeping.
corrections: *** VERSION: our records and the user's tracking table both say 'arXiv:2604.05991v1'. The PDF on disk is v2 (2 Jul 2026). Cite v2.

Target is a VEHICLE, not a drone. Diffraction is the paper's whole subject (147 'diffract*' hits), which is why the user's table double-fills that column.
It ships an open-source fork: https://github.com/AinurZiga/sionna-RT-reflectivity (cited as accessed 2026-03-31). Relevant to our OPENSOURCE.md.

quotes.text: We consider a monostatic ISAC system where a single BS simultaneously performs sensing and communication using separate transmit and receive antenna arrays with Nt and Nr elements, respectively.

quotes.supports: their bistatic extension is a remark, not a result

In the PDF 'Diffraction' occurs only TWICE, both times as one word in a single figure legend listing Sionna's ray interaction types ('Line-of-sight / Specular reflection / Diffuse reflection / Refraction / Diffraction'). entries.short: Pasquale et al., SagittaSBR - BVH-accelerated SBR
entries.venue_as_printed_in_pdf: NONE - arXiv stamp 'arXiv:2604.09243v1 [cs.CE] 10 Apr 2026', plus an author note naming ICCS 2026
entries.status_from_pdf: EXTENDED PREPRINT of an accepted paper. Verbatim: 'Note. This manuscript is an extended version of the paper accepted at the 26th International Conference on Computational Science (ICCS 2026).'
entries.geometry: MONOSTATIC ONLY (explicitly); PEC sphere + a complex aircraft

quotes.text: We validate against analytical Mie solutions for a perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) sphere and demonstrate applicability to a complex aircraft geometry for monostatic radar cross-section prediction.
quotes.supports: *** same validation strategy as our V2 (kernel vs analytic reference on a PEC sphere)

quotes.text: A bistatic scattering calculation would require a visibility function to account for shadow regions between the reflection points and the final receiver. In a monostatic configuration this can be omitted, since the predominantly scattering surfaces are by assumption visible to the co-located launcher and receiver.
quotes.supports: *** EXTERNAL PRIMARY-SOURCE CONFIRMATION of our own 'bistatic needs more than an obliquity change' limitation

quotes.text: A known modeling limitation of classical GO+PO SBR is the absence of diffraction mechanisms, which can be important near edges, tips, or shadow boundaries.
quotes.supports: *** lets us state our own no-diffraction limitation with an external citation instead of only self-assertion

quotes.text: the monostatic RCS is sigma = 4*pi*|A|^2, which is evaluated in m2 and typically expressed in dBsm as 10 log10(sigma).
quotes.supports: definition parity with our kernel

entries.verdict: *** STATUS CORRECTED and the paper is more useful to us than recorded.
corrections: Cite as 'arXiv:2604.09243v1, extended version of a paper accepted at ICCS 2026' - NOT as an ICCS 2026 paper simpliciter, and not as a bare preprint either.
cautions: Target is an aircraft (Sagitta), PEC, not a drone. Open source: https://github.com/marco-pas/SagittaSBR.

entries.geometry: ACTIVE MONOSTATIC, full-duplex BS

quotes.text: A new mathematical model for UAV micro-Doppler in monostatic ISAC systems is proposed.
quotes.supports: geometry

quotes.text: The BS is equipped with separate antennas that enable full-duplex operation, allowing it to transmit and receive signals simultaneously.
quotes.supports: it is the transmitter - the toll our reports describe

quotes.text: During DL slots, the BS utilizes all physical downlink shared channel (PDSCH) signals as sensing symbols, resulting in the shortest pulse repetition interval (PRI) of 33.3 microseconds.
quotes.supports: *** PRF = 30 kHz achieved by owning the transmitter and using DATA symbols

quotes.text: To ensure that these features are preserved, the pulse repetition frequency (PRF) must be at least twice the maximum micro-Doppler frequency, i.e., PRF >= 2 f_mD_max, where the maximum micro-Doppler frequency is given by f_mD_max = 2*pi*f_r*L/lambda.
quotes.supports: *** the SAME Nyquist-on-PRF law family as our V1 - published, monostatic form

quotes.text: For example, using our hardware test parameters (fr = 80 r/s and L = 0.5 m), we obtain fmD = 2934 Hz, which requires a PRF of at least 5868 Hz (corresponding to a PRI of less than 1.7 x 10^-4 s).
quotes.supports: a concrete published PRF requirement to place beside our table

entries.verdict: *** IMPORTANT NUANCE FOR V4, not a contradiction.
corrections: *** V4 says '3GPP sub-6 CSI-RS caps at 500 Hz -> 10.71 m/s ... covers 0 of 5 airframes'. That is true FOR REFERENCE SIGNALS. A09 shows the published escape route: a system that OWNS the transmitter uses PDSCH data symbols and reaches PRI 33.3 us (PRF ~30 kHz). When we state V4 we must say 'the 500 Hz cap binds systems restricted to CSI-RS; monostatic systems that own the transmitter bypass it via PDSCH (A09) or via non-uniform sparse recovery (LaSen)'. Otherwise V4 overstates.
